findings.title: SQL Injection via Unsanitized ORDER BY Parameter
findings.impact: SQL injection allows attackers to read/modify/delete arbitrary database records via the sort parameter in the /invoices endpoint
findings.evidence: const rows = await db.query(`SELECT * FROM invoices WHERE owner_id = $1 ORDER BY ${order}`, [req.user.id]); where order = req.query.order || 'created_at' and no validation exists
findings.recommendation: Replace dynamic query construction with a whitelist of allowed columns: const ALLOWED = {'created_at': 'created_at', 'amount': 'amount'}; const column = ALLOWED[req.query.order] || 'created_at';

findings.title: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) via Unescaped HTML in Invoice Notes
findings.impact: Stored XSS vulnerability allowing attackers to inject arbitrary JavaScript into invoice notes viewed by other users
findings.evidence:
function invoiceNote(note) { return `
${note}
`; } - uses note directly without HTML escaping
findings.recommendation:
Apply HTML escaping: return `
${escapeHtml(note)}
;` (escapeHtml is already imported in this module)

findings.title: Indirect Object Reference (IDOR) in Invoice Detail Endpoint
findings.impact: Unauthorized access to invoices: users can read invoices belonging to other customers by guessing or enumerating invoice IDs
findings.evidence: router.get('/invoices/:id', ...) executes SELECT * FROM invoices WHERE id = $1 without checking owner_id, while the /receipts/:id endpoint on line 13 correctly includes AND owner_id = $2
findings.recommendation: Add owner_id check to WHERE clause: 'SELECT * FROM invoices WHERE id = $1 AND owner_id = $2', [req.params.id, req.user.id]. Note: this assumes req.user.id is available from authenticated context.

findings.title: JWT Token Verification Bypass
findings.impact: Authentication bypass: attackers can forge JWT tokens without a valid signature as jwt.decode() does not verify the token signature
findings.evidence: const claims = jwt.decode(bearer); - uses jwt.decode() which only parses the token without verifying the signature against a secret key
findings.recommendation: Use jwt.verify() instead: const claims = jwt.verify(bearer, process.env.JWT_SECRET || 'secret'); and wrap in try/catch for invalid tokens

findings.title: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) via Redirect in fetchLogo
findings.impact: An attacker-controlled logoUrl can redirect to internal services (localhost, internal IPs) or sensitive endpoints, leading to SSRF attacks
findings.evidence: const response = await fetch(url, { redirect: 'follow' }); - allows the server to follow redirects to any destination including internal services
findings.recommendation: Set redirect: 'error' to reject redirects: const response = await fetch(url, { redirect: 'error' }); or validate the final URL is still on assets.example.com

findings.title: Undefined Return Value in tagRequest Function
findings.impact: Function returns undefined instead of the tagged request object, breaking metric tagging and returning wrong data to callers
findings.evidence: function tagRequest(req, metrics) { ... return req.session.user; } where req.session.user is never set by any prior code (req.session is never initialized)
findings.recommendation: Return the claims object or the user info: return { id: claims.sub, role: claims.role }; or remove this function if unused
